cases.description: Heart failure discharge with four follow-ups.
COPD discharge, numbered plan, red-flag line must not become a follow-up.
Diabetes discharge with synonyms (blood test, primary care).
Post-op discharge that explicitly says no cardiology follow-up.
Pneumonia discharge that says home care is not needed.
AF discharge with a repeat bloodwork instruction.
The demo story: discharge, Day 3 self-report, Day 7 clinic booking, Day 10 conflicting date, Day 12 medication question.
Patient says they went to the family doctor; that is evidence, not proof.
Patient says bloodwork is done. Must stay open pending lab results.
Clinic confirms cardiology; days later the patient names a different date.
Patient repeats the clinic-confirmed date. No false conflict.
Weeks after the clinic booked cardiology, the patient asks when it is.
Patient says the clinic moved the visit; the new date is a claim to verify, not a fact.
'I haven't gone to the family doctor yet' must keep the loop open.
Dosing question must be declined and escalated to a clinician.
New chest pain during a routine check-in must escalate.
Patient denies symptoms; nothing should escalate.
Three separate sessions about different follow-ups; all must be remembered.
A friendly call that mentions no follow-ups must not drop any open loop.
Patient says the clinic cancelled; cancellation needs coordinator sign-off.
Caregiver reports a visit and asks a dosing question in the same call.
